config.title: Orders List Page

intro.title: Orders List Page
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build an orders list page that displays a collection of orders in a clean, organized table. You'll learn how to use Angular components to structure your page and TypeScript to define the data model for your orders. The main technologies involved are Angular components, TypeScript interfaces, and Angular's template syntax for displaying data. By the end, you'll have a functional page that shows order details like ID, customer name, and status in a structured format.
intro.usecase: The orders list page pattern is fundamental to e-commerce platforms, admin dashboards, and business management systems. You'll see this in Shopify's order management interface, Amazon Seller Central's order tracking, and restaurant POS systems displaying pending orders. As a developer, you'll implement similar pages for customer support portals to view ticket queues, inventory systems to track shipments, and financial platforms to monitor transactions. This pattern combines data fetching, state management, and user interaction in a practical, reusable component structure.

objectives: Construct a new Angular component using the CLI to serve as the orders list page
Apply Angular routing to define a route that maps a URL path to the orders component
Implement a TypeScript interface to define the structure of an order object with required properties
Utilize array iteration with *ngFor to display a list of order items in the template
Assign mock order data to a component property to simulate API data retrieval
Access component properties in the template using interpolation to display order details
Modify the component template to structure order information with appropriate HTML elements
Use Angular's built-in date pipe to format order dates for display
Apply CSS classes to style the orders list for visual presentation
Control template rendering with *ngIf to handle empty order lists gracefully
Define a click handler method to navigate to order details when an order is selected
Implement property binding to connect the click handler to order list items

steps.title: Generate the orders component
steps.instruction: Run the Angular CLI command to generate a new component named 'orders'.
steps.hint: Use the ng generate component command with the component name 'orders'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example command to generate a component named 'orders'
ng generate component orders
steps.seedCode:
// Run the Angular CLI command to generate the orders component
// ng generate component orders
steps.expectedOutcome: The Angular CLI will create the orders component with its TypeScript, HTML, CSS, and spec files.
successCriteria: The command should execute successfully and create the component files in the correct directory.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully generated the orders component using the Angular CLI.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the correct Angular CLI command format: ng generate component orders.
steps.feedbackWrong: The command didn't execute as expected. Try running 'ng generate component orders' in your terminal.

steps.title: Import Component and OnInit from '@angular/core'
steps.instruction: In the orders.component.ts file, add an import statement to import Component and OnInit from '@angular/core'.
steps.hint: Use the import keyword followed by the symbols you want to import in curly braces, then specify the module path.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing from @angular/core
import { Component, OnInit } from '@angular/core';
steps.expectedOutcome: The orders.component.ts file will have the necessary imports for creating an Angular component with lifecycle hooks.
successCriteria: The import statement should correctly import both Component and OnInit from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported Component and OnInit. These are essential Angular decorators and interfaces for component creation.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing both Component and OnInit from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is incorrect. Check that you're importing Component and OnInit from '@angular/core'.

steps.title: Define the OrdersComponent class with OnInit
steps.instruction: Define the OrdersComponent class that implements the OnInit interface. The class should be exported and include the ngOnInit method.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator above the class definition. The class should implement OnInit and include ngOnInit() method.
steps.expectedOutcome: The OrdersComponent class is defined with proper TypeScript syntax, implements OnInit, and includes the ngOnInit method.
successCriteria: The code should contain: 1) @Component decorator with selector, templateUrl, and styleUrls, 2) export class OrdersComponent implements OnInit, 3) constructor, 4) ngOnInit() method.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the OrdersComponent class with proper Angular structure and implemented the OnInit interface.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Check that you have: 1) @Component decorator with the three properties, 2) class implements OnInit, 3) constructor, and 4) ngOnInit() method.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component class definition is incomplete or incorrect. Make sure to implement the OnInit interface and include all required parts.

steps.title: Add the @Component decorator with selector and template
steps.instruction: Add the @Component decorator above your OrdersComponent class. Configure it with selector: 'app-orders' and templateUrl: './orders.component.html'.
steps.hint: Place @Component({ selector: 'app-orders', templateUrl: './orders.component.html' }) directly above your class definition.
steps.expectedOutcome: The OrdersComponent class now has the @Component decorator with the required metadata, making it a proper Angular component.
successCriteria: The code includes @Component decorator with selector 'app-orders' and templateUrl './orders.component.html' above the class.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the @Component decorator with the correct selector and template URL. This configures your component's metadata so Angular knows how to use it.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your @Component decorator has both 'selector' and 'templateUrl' properties with the exact values 'app-orders' and './orders.component.html'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The @Component decorator is missing or incorrectly configured. Make sure to add @Component({ selector: 'app-orders', templateUrl: './orders.component.html' }) above your OrdersComponent class.

steps.title: Define the Order interface
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named 'Order' with the following properties: 'id' (number), 'customerName' (string), 'total' (number), and 'status' (string). Place this interface above the OrdersComponent class.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions. Each property should have a type annotation.
steps.expectedOutcome: An Order interface is defined with the correct properties and types, ready to be used for typing order data.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the Order interface with all required properties and proper TypeScript types.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the interface is missing some required properties or has incorrect types. Check that all four properties (id, customerName, total, status) are defined with the correct types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Order interface wasn't defined correctly. Make sure to use the 'interface' keyword, name it 'Order', and include all four properties with their TypeScript types.

steps.title: Initialize orders array property
steps.instruction: Inside the OrdersComponent class, create a property named 'orders' of type 'Order[]' and initialize it as an empty array.
steps.hint: Add a class property with the correct type annotation and assign it an empty array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a typed property to store orders data, ready for later population.
successCriteria: The component class contains a property named 'orders' with type 'Order[]' initialized to an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully declared and initialized the orders property with the correct type.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the property is named 'orders', has type 'Order[]', and is initialized as an empty array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The orders property is missing or incorrect. It should be a class property with type 'Order[]' and an empty array initializer.

steps.title: Implement ngOnInit lifecycle method
steps.instruction: Inside the ngOnInit method, populate the orders array with at least two sample order objects matching the Order interface.
steps.hint: Assign an array of order objects to this.orders. Each object should have id, customerName, and total properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ngOnInit method should initialize the orders array with sample data, making it ready for display in the template.
successCriteria: The ngOnInit method contains code that assigns an array of at least two order objects to this.orders.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented ngOnInit to populate the orders array with sample data. This ensures the component has data ready when it initializes.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're assigning the array directly to this.orders inside ngOnInit. Also verify each order object has all required properties: id, customerName, and total.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ngOnInit method should contain code that assigns sample order data to this.orders. Try adding something like: this.orders = [{ id: 1, customerName: 'Customer A', total: 100 }, { id: 2, customerName: 'Customer B', total: 200 }];

steps.title: Create the orders template structure
steps.instruction: In the orders.component.html file, create a container div with a header and a basic table structure for displaying orders.
steps.hint: Start with a div element, add an h2 header inside it, then create a table element with thead and tbody sections.
steps.analogousExample:
Orders List

ID Customer Total
steps.expectedOutcome: The component's template should have a container div with a header and a table structure ready to display order data.
successCriteria: The template should contain: a div element, an h2 header with text, a table element with thead and tbody sections, and table headers for ID, Customer, and Total.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the basic HTML structure for the orders list page with a container, header, and table skeleton.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your template includes all required elements: a div container, an h2 header, a table with thead and tbody, and table headers for ID, Customer, and Total.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template structure doesn't match what's needed. Please create a div container with a header and a table structure that includes thead and tbody sections.

steps.title: Add table headers
steps.instruction: Inside the template string, add a <table> element with a <thead> section containing table headers for ID, Customer, Total, and Status columns.
steps.hint: Use <th> elements inside a <tr> within the <thead> to create column headers.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of table headers in an Angular template template: `
ID Customer Total Status
`
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template now includes a table structure with headers for the orders data columns.
successCriteria: The template must contain a <table> element with a <thead> section that has four <th> elements for ID, Customer, Total, and Status.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the table headers. This creates the structure needed to display your orders data in a table format.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have all four headers (ID, Customer, Total, Status) inside a <thead> within a <table> element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet have the required table headers. Check that you've added a <table> with <thead> containing <th> elements for each column.

steps.title: Use *ngFor to iterate over orders
steps.instruction: In the component's template, add a table row (<tr>) element with the *ngFor directive to iterate over the 'orders' array. Create a table row for each order in the array.
steps.hint: Use the syntax *ngFor="let order of orders" on a <tr> element. This will generate one table row for each order in the orders array.
steps.analogousExample: • {{ item.name }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The component's template will have a table row element that uses Angular's *ngFor structural directive to loop through the orders array.
successCriteria: The template should contain a <tr> element with the *ngFor directive that iterates over the 'orders' array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the *ngFor directive to iterate over the orders array. This will generate a table row for each order when the array is populated.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added the *ngFor directive to a <tr> element and used the correct syntax: *ngFor="let order of orders".
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't contain the *ngFor directive on a table row element. Remember to add <tr *ngFor="let order of orders"> to iterate through the orders array.

steps.title: Display order data in table cells
steps.instruction: Inside the table row template, add table cells (<td>) that display each order's id, customerName, and total properties using interpolation.
steps.hint: Use interpolation syntax {{ order.property }} inside <td> elements to display the data.
steps.analogousExample: {{ item.id }} {{ item.name }} {{ item.price }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The table will have three columns populated with order data when the orders array contains items.
successCriteria: Use interpolation {{ order.id }} in first cell
Use interpolation {{ order.customerName }} in second cell
Use interpolation {{ order.total }} in third cell
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully added table cells that display the order data using interpolation. The table will now show actual order information when data is available.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have all three table cells with the correct interpolation syntax for each order property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The table cells aren't displaying the order data correctly. Check that you're using interpolation syntax {{ }} and accessing the order properties properly.

steps.title: Add CSS styling for the orders table
steps.instruction: Create a CSS file named 'orders.component.css' and add styling rules to make the orders table visually appealing. Style the table, table headers, and table rows.
steps.hint: Create a new file in the same directory as your component. Use CSS selectors like 'table', 'th', and 'tr' to target elements.
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS file is created with styling rules that improve the visual appearance of the orders table.
successCriteria: The CSS file should contain at least one rule for the table element, one for table headers (th), and one for table rows (tr).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the CSS file and added styling rules to make the orders table more visually appealing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the CSS file, but it needs more styling rules. Make sure to include rules for the table, headers, and rows.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS file wasn't created correctly or doesn't contain the expected styling rules. Please create 'orders.component.css' and add CSS rules for the table, headers, and rows.
